raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

Fixes #61632. The Olmo3 tool parser drops the tool call in non-streaming mode when a string argument contains `</function_calls>`. Streaming handles the same output correctly.

## Claims

- Non-streaming `Olmo3PythonicToolParser.extract_tool_calls` no longer treats a `</function_calls>` inside a string argument as the end of the block.
- Streaming and non-streaming now return the same tool calls for this input.
- Behaviour is unchanged for normal output, for output without tags, and for output with an unclosed tag.

## Validation

Added three cases to `tests/tool_parsers/test_olmo3_tool_parser.py`: streaming, non-streaming, and non-streaming with a second parallel call.

```
pytest tests/tool_parsers/test_olmo3_tool_parser.py tests/tool_parsers/test_pythonic_tool_parser.py
41 passed
```

Without the parser change, the two new non-streaming cases fail. The streaming case already passed.

## Details

**Root cause:** the wrapper was stripped with `re.search(r"<function_calls>(.*?)</function_calls>", ...)`. The non-greedy match ends at the first closing tag, even inside a quoted argument. The remaining text is no longer valid Python, so the parser falls back to returning everything as `content`.

**Fix:** `_strip_function_calls_tags` tries each `</function_calls>` in order and keeps the first body that `ast.parse`s once joined into a list (the same newline join as before). If none parses, it falls back to the first closing tag, which is the previous behaviour.

**Not a greedy `(.*)`:** a greedy match would join two separate `<function_calls>` blocks into one unparseable body. Today the first block parses, and this change keeps that.

The newline join is moved into `_to_call_list` unchanged, so the bodies being tried go through exactly the same transformation as the final parse. #60433 and #60436 change that join (newlines inside strings). They are independent of this fix and may need a trivial rebase against it.

Same bug class as #45167 (Hermes, `</tool_call>` inside a JSON string).

@smiyamoto3 Thanks for testing this so carefully!

1. Good catch on the `MemoryError`. I reproduced it on Python 3.13, switched to `except Exception`, and added `test_deeply_nested_tool_call_falls_back_to_content`, which fails without the fix.
2. While looking at this, I noticed that trying every closing tag is quadratic: a string full of fake `</function_calls>` tags took ~11 s for 8000 tags. The search now tries at most 16 candidates (`MAX_CLOSING_TAG_CANDIDATES`). Past that it falls back to content, like main does. `test_many_closing_tags_in_string_parse_count_is_bounded` checks the number of parses.
3. On #60436: agreed. If it lands first, I'll rebase and check candidates with `_parse_newline_separated_calls`. If this one lands first, I'm happy to leave a note on #60436.
4. Thanks for checking the larger deltas. I also added a streaming test where a delta ends right after the in-string `</function_calls>`.

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

Two problems. Tested at e0f2591dc7.

The new `ast.parse` in `_strip_function_calls_tags` runs before the regex check and only catches `SyntaxError`/`ValueError` ([L96-L98](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/e0f2591dc71e0a9414951f50f3b682e565f50716/vllm/tool_parsers/olmo3_tool_parser.py#L96-L98)). A deeply nested body like `"<function_calls>f(a=" + "-" * 7000 + "1)</function_calls>"` raises `MemoryError` there and fails the request, while main returns it as content. Could you catch `Exception` there? That fixed it for me.

This also conflicts with #60436. Whichever lands second should check candidates with #60436's `_parse_newline_separated_calls`, otherwise a multi-line call with `</function_calls>` in a string falls back to content in non-streaming. I tried that swap on a merged branch and the olmo3 tests pass.

The new tests also pass when I group the stream into bigger deltas.
Thanks for adding the cap, LGTM!

Verified this offline at the parser level: the false-marker handling resolves #61632 in both modes — the added test covers the issue's exact sample, and my probe battery on this head agrees. On the full sweep, this head's output differs from `main` only on the false-marker family and the combined sample below; every other probe, controls included, is byte-identical.

The one shape worth adding to the map is the two reported triggers combined — a false closing tag *and* a real newline in the same value:

```python
"<function_calls>write_file(path='notes.txt', content='End with </function_calls> and\na newline.')</function_calls>"
```

How the heads score on it:

| head | non-streaming | streaming |
|---|---|---|
| `main` (262eefc9f2) | whole output as content, 0 calls | char-by-char: one call, argument JSON cut off mid-string, never closed; as one chunk: silent |
| this PR (a89ecc8b7d) | call extracted; value ships with the newline joined into `", "` | unchanged from `main` on both feeds |
| #60433 (17235bd654) | whole output as content, 0 calls | extracted correctly, value byte-exact on both feeds |
| #60436 (2d99c77a77) | whole output as content, 0 calls | extracted correctly, value byte-exact on both feeds |

On this head the candidate loop rejects the false tag and lands on the real one — but the payload passes through the old line join on the way in, and the joined body still parses, so the call ships with the value silently mangled: `End with </function_calls> and, a newline.` where the model wrote a real line break. So no single head covers the combined shape: this one extracts-and-corrupts, the two newline PRs fix the streaming side but drop it non-streaming.

That is the behavioral counterpart of the point @smiyamoto3 made on the #60436 thread: the candidate check here runs on the old line join, so "whichever merges second should run that check through `_parse_newline_separated_calls`". The combined sample is the concrete case behind it, and with this PR now approved, the datapoint is for whoever decides the order — this sample is the ready-made test for how the combination behaves once the second of the two lands.

The tests added here cover the issue sample, the deep-nesting fallback, and the bounded candidate count; the newline combination isn't among them. Happy to share the probe.

(These runs were AI-assisted; raw logs for all five SHAs are available.)

+    default_tokenizer: TokenizerLike,

+    tool_parser: ToolParser = ToolParserManager.get_tool_parser("olmo3")(

+    # The first delta ends with a "</function_calls>" that is inside a string.
+    model_output_deltas = [
+        "<function_calls>write_file(path='README.md', "
+        "content='Calls are wrapped in <function_calls>...</function_calls>",
+        ".')</function_calls>",
+    ]

+    assert len(reconstructor.tool_calls) == 1
+    assert reconstructor.tool_calls[0].function == CLOSING_TAG_IN_STRING_FUNCTION_CALL
+
+
+def test_deeply_nested_tool_call_falls_back_to_content(
+    default_tokenizer: TokenizerLike,
+):
+    tool_parser: ToolParser = ToolParserManager.get_tool_parser("olmo3")(
+        default_tokenizer
+    )
+    # Too deep for ast.parse, which raises MemoryError instead of SyntaxError.
+    model_output = "<function_calls>f(a=" + "-" * 7000 + "1)</function_calls>"
+
+    content, tool_calls = run_tool_extraction(
+        tool_parser, model_output, streaming=False
+    )
+
+    assert content == model_output
+    assert len(tool_calls) == 0
+
+
+def test_many_closing_tags_in_string_parse_count_is_bounded(
+    default_tokenizer: TokenizerLike,
+):
+    tool_parser: ToolParser = ToolParserManager.get_tool_parser("olmo3")(
+        default_tokenizer
+    )
+    # An unterminated string full of fake closing tags. Trying each one
+    # would parse the body thousands of times.
+    model_output = "<function_calls>f(a='" + "x</function_calls>" * 5000
+
+    with patch(
+        "vllm.tool_parsers.olmo3_tool_parser.ast.parse", wraps=ast.parse
+    ) as mock_parse:
+        content, tool_calls = run_tool_extraction(
+            tool_parser, model_output, streaming=False
+        )
+
+    assert content == model_output
+    assert len(tool_calls) == 0
+    # The candidate search, plus at most one parse in extract_tool_calls.
+    assert mock_parse.call_count <= tool_parser.MAX_CLOSING_TAG_CANDIDATES + 1
+

         re.DOTALL,
     )
 
+    # How many "</function_calls>" tags to try as the real closing tag.
+    MAX_CLOSING_TAG_CANDIDATES = 16
+
     def __init__(
         self,
         tokenizer: PreTrainedTokenizerBase,
@@ -67,22 +70,51 @@ def current_tool_index(self) -> int:
     def current_tool_index(self, value: int) -> None:
         self.current_tool_id = value
 
+    @staticmethod
+    def _to_call_list(text: str) -> str:
+        """Make the newline separated function calls into a list."""
+        lines = [line.strip() for line in text.splitlines() if line.strip()]
+        return f"[{', '.join(lines)}]"
+
+    @classmethod
+    def _strip_function_calls_tags(cls, model_output: str) -> str:
+        """Return the body of the <function_calls> block.
+
+        A string argument may itself contain "</function_calls>", so the
+        first closing tag is not necessarily the real one. Use the first
+        closing tag whose body parses as Python, and fall back to the first
+        closing tag otherwise. Only the first few closing tags are tried,
+        since each try parses the whole body.
+        """
+        start = model_output.find("<function_calls>")
+        if start == -1:
+            return model_output
+        body_start = start + len("<function_calls>")
+        first_end = model_output.find("</function_calls>", body_start)
+        if first_end == -1:
+            return model_output
+        end = first_end
+        for _ in range(cls.MAX_CLOSING_TAG_CANDIDATES):
+            if end == -1:
+                break
+            body = model_output[body_start:end]
+            try:
+                ast.parse(cls._to_call_list(body))
+                return body.strip()
+            # Not only SyntaxError: deeply nested input can raise
+            # MemoryError or RecursionError from ast.parse.
+            except Exception:
+                end = model_output.find("</function_calls>", end + 1)
+        return model_output[body_start:first_end].strip()
+

     ) -> ExtractedToolCallInformation:
         """Extract the tool calls from a complete model response."""
         original_model_output = model_output

-        )
